what_it_does: Severe rain counts only if at least this many of the creek's working rain gauges are at Very heavy or above (1 = no confirmation). A creek with fewer working rain gauges needs all of them.

A rain gauge counts as 'no recent data' if it has reported nothing for this long while another rain gauge on the same creek recorded rain. (Replaces RAIN_FREQ_FRESH_MIN: gauges report only every 1-12 h when dry, so a plain age limit would flag them all; otherwise a rain gauge counts as working if it reported within GAUGE_QUIET_HOURS.)

Creek level trend (rising / steady / falling) is the fitted slope over this many minutes. Gauges that report only when the level changes hold their last value; gauges that report on a schedule less often than this use their last two readings (see TREND_MAX_WINDOW_MIN).
Longest window for the trend on gauges that report less often than TREND_WINDOW_MIN (e.g. hourly); older readings give no trend
A slope smaller than this either way counts as Steady
The rising-tide line shows when the next high tide is within this many hours
POLICY: whether severe rain or rising fast can make a creek without flood levels "Be ready" (1) or only "Stay alert" (0)
